overlapRules.rule: One actual-dispatch inheritance predicate; all clauses retained
One use/disposition/result/extra-research predicate; all clauses retained
One learning-writeback predicate per entry/version/role; all clauses retained
One schedule-window recurrence/exception predicate; all clauses retained
Detailed attachment predicates supply broad summary; residuals remain
Detailed logistics predicates plus broad residuals; not all items merged
Scope summaries reuse exact fact predicates; distinct amounts/regimes/residuals remain
Scope specializations reuse matching predicates; distinct selection/publisher/window clauses remain
Lifecycle summary reuses exact events; distinct stages/triggers remain
Reuse identical authority facts; generic meaning/local powers/form remain distinct
Share evidence; do not merge distinct outcome/vote/join facts
One reusable asset; distinct official-term and candidate-cycle binding verification
Reuse public witnesses; readiness never adds civic points

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Target scope — The manifest names the exact states, districts, ZIPs, record families, and exclusions; counts reconcile with the input inventory.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Running release — Runtime heartbeat and process provenance identify the deployed code containing required fixes; files on disk alone do not pass.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Database access — A normal runner cycle reaches its required production stores; connection errors are recorded and handled by bounded retry or a clear failure outcome.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Normal dispatch — At least one eligible normal task is dispatched and finishes with a durable result; an isolated harness is labeled separately.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Scout inheritance — An actual dispatched scout’s captured input contains the expected applicable knowledge; its actions show how that knowledge was used.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Effective spending control — Admission and spending reservation obey the same approved effective ceiling; model and paid-search costs or unmeasured costs are disclosed.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Schedule and wake behavior — The owner knows which lanes run now, during quiet periods, and overnight; intended work is not silently blocked by schedule or stale settings.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Safe publication — Invalid, incomplete, or conflicting candidates cannot replace valid data; existing accepted data is preserved where available and its age remains visible.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Reader path — For each enabled record family, an accepted example reaches its intended public view with correct identity and context; missing family paths are named blockers for that family.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Honest status — Unknown is distinct from zero, failure from no records, and source delay from work not attempted; Admin reflects recorded decisions and their times.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Access and privacy — Acquisition uses permitted sources and held permissions; no evasion or secret/private personal data appears in outputs.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Overnight continuity — Power, sleep settings, connectivity, scheduled launcher, and recovery procedure are checked; no folder move or competing manual runner can disrupt the run.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Single ownership — One launch owner controls the manifest and dispatch; workers do not duplicate state assignments or race promotions.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Review boundary — The agreed scout attempt/spend boundary has a working way to stop further admissions for review; merely writing a reminder is insufficient.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: ZIP identity — Postal code, state, postal classification, reference source, and reference date match the target inventory.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Postal and civic distinction — Postal city labels are not presented as proof of municipal government or jurisdiction.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Boundary provenance — Every used division or boundary has an identified source, version, and effective period.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Resolution method — Each result says whether it uses an address, ZIP center, ZIP overlap, or another documented method.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Uncertainty — Bodies that may govern part of a ZIP are labeled accordingly; exact applicability is not asserted from overlap alone.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Split ZIP — When a ZIP touches multiple jurisdictions, all supported alternatives are recorded and narrowing requires the appropriate address information.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Government layers — State, county or equivalent, municipality or township, and unincorporated status are resolved or explicitly unresolved.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Legislative districts — Federal and state districts are linked using the boundary version applicable to the represented term or election.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: School districts — Where present, elementary, secondary, and unified district responsibilities are distinguished and supported by boundary evidence.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Special districts — Known service districts have a defined territory and function; inclusion is supported rather than inferred from a mailing address.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Tribal and overlapping authority — Where relevant, overlapping jurisdiction and governmental roles are described from authoritative sources without assuming equivalence to municipal government.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: PO Box or UNIQUE ZIP — A nonresidential postal code has a documented handling decision; no residential jurisdiction is fabricated.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Boundary change — Redistricting, annexation, merger, and dissolution preserve effective dates and do not silently alter historical records.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Geographic deduplication — Stable division identities prevent the same government from being counted twice through different ZIPs or aliases.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Official identity — Name, stable ID, government type, official source, and geography are recorded.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Governing organization — The main council, commission, board, or chamber is identified and linked to its government.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Official directory review — The current official board, commission, and department directories are checked and their review evidence is saved.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Legal enumeration — Available charter, code, or establishing records are checked for bodies missing from the directory; unresolved discrepancies remain open.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Body classification — Governing, advisory, administrative, adjudicative, and oversight roles are distinguished where supported.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Parent relationships — Each body links to its parent government; joint bodies may have multiple parents rather than a forced single owner.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Plain-language purpose — Each government or body has a sourced explanation of its role without unsupported claims about authority.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Official entry point — Official website or verified publisher and a public contact channel are recorded, or their missing state is documented.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Authority citation — Where decision-making or financial authority is described, the relevant charter, statute, ordinance, or delegation supports it.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Operational status — Active, dissolved, renamed, dormant, and unconfirmed bodies are distinguished with dates and evidence.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Inventory denominator — Expected count and source are recorded where known; otherwise discovery remains explicitly open with checked sources listed.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Dependent organizations — Dependent districts and departments are not double-counted as independent governments.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Service directory — Office hours, service responsibilities, accessible contact options, and language assistance are recorded where published.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Historic structure — Predecessor and successor bodies retain dated relationships for historical searches.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Seat identity — The office or seat exists independently of its holder and has a stable identifier and official label.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Role and area — The office’s function, organization, and represented area are linked correctly.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Selection method — Elected, appointed, selected by colleagues, and ex officio roles are distinguished from official evidence.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Current occupancy — The current holder, verified vacancy, or unresolved occupancy is recorded; a missing name never automatically means vacancy.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Person identity — Names and identifiers resolve to the right person across sources; unresolved same-name matches are not merged.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Tenure — Current service start and expected end are recorded where officially established; uncertainty is explicit.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Holdover or interim service — A nominal term end does not remove a person still lawfully serving; interim and acting roles are labeled.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Official page — A verified official profile or roster supports the officeholder relationship.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Official contact — Published office contact channels are captured separately from campaign and personal channels.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Seat count — Multi-seat and at-large bodies reconcile their roster with the number of authorized seats; unidentified seats remain visible.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Party context — Party is included only where relevant and sourced; ballot label, affiliation, endorsement, and registration are not conflated.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Committee membership — Published current committee assignments include role, committee, and period; chair and ordinary member are distinct.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Ex officio membership — Membership on behalf of another office identifies that relationship and avoids inventing a separate person.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Judicial and retention office — Judicial offices and retention-election links use their actual appointment and election rules.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Election linkage — An office with an applicable upcoming contest links to that contest and the correct seat or term.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Career history — Previous memberships and name changes retain dates and evidence without replacing current service.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Publisher route — The body’s authoritative calendar, API, feed, portal, or notice source is identified and linked to the correct body.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Route identity — Known vendor tenant, body ID, exact endpoint, and relevant parameters are verified and reusable by workers.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Bounded enumeration — All pages, date ranges, and result limits needed for the declared acquisition window are handled; an arbitrary first page is not complete.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Cadence — Regular schedule or irregular notice practice is recorded with exceptions where officially published.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Meeting identity — Each meeting has a stable ID, correct body, and a deduplication key or equivalent verified identity.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Date — Calendar date is supported by the official source and is not inferred from upload time.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Time — Start time and time zone are preserved; a missing time is not replaced with midnight.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Location — Physical venue or verified remote-only status is recorded; unresolved venue mappings remain failed requirements.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Remote access — Published meeting URL, access instructions, and phone participation details are captured when offered.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Meeting state — Scheduled, canceled, postponed, rescheduled, and concluded states match the source.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Rescheduling link — A replacement meeting links to the old instance so both are not advertised as upcoming.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Source link — Readers can reach the meeting’s official listing or document and see its provenance.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Special meetings — Special, emergency, joint, workshop, and study sessions inside the window are included when in the body’s official notices.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Restricted session — Publicly announced executive or closed sessions retain public metadata; unavailable private proceedings are not invented or acquired improperly.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Empty-result handling — Zero extracted meetings is investigated against the source and window before being treated as a verified empty schedule.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Publisher horizon — If future dates are not yet published, the source’s observed or declared horizon is shown rather than claiming indefinite future coverage.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Recurrence expansion — Recurring schedules respect exceptions, time zones, and cancellations; inferred instances are distinguishable from confirmed notices.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Calendar export — Exported event data preserves identity, updates, cancellations, and time zones when the product offers export.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Agenda availability — For meetings with published agendas, the official agenda link and publication state are captured.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Agenda acquisition — The published agenda document is retrieved and usable; a filename or link alone does not prove readable content.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Agenda extraction — Text or OCR extraction preserves meaningful order and references; extraction uncertainty is visible.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Attachments — Published attachments promised by the active contract are enumerated and linked to their agenda item or meeting.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Revised agenda — Amendments, addenda, and replacement agendas preserve versions and identify the current one.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Minutes — Published minutes link to the correct meeting and distinguish draft from approved minutes.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Recordings — Published audio or video has a working official link and correct meeting identity.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Meeting actions — Published motions, decisions, and outcomes retain their context and source references.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Member votes — When recorded votes are published and within scope, member, motion, position, and outcome are linked without inference from party or attendance.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Missing publication — Expected but unpublished records carry an evidenced publication state, next check, and overdue status where applicable.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Scans — A scanned source is retained with extracted text and quality checks; OCR output is not treated as flawless evidence.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Searchable transcript — Where promised, transcripts link statements to speakers and timestamps, label automated transcription, and preserve the source recording.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Document relationships — Supporting packets, ordinances, exhibits, and attachments can be followed across meeting versions.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Session identity — Legislature, chamber, session, year, and regular or special session are recorded distinctly.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Member mapping — Source member IDs resolve to the correct people, seats, and service dates.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Bill identity — Bill number, jurisdiction, session, and official link are preserved; repeated numbers across years do not collide.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Bill context — Each displayed vote has an intelligible bill title or official subject, not only a hash or internal ID.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Motion or question — The action being voted on is preserved, distinguishing passage, amendment, procedure, and other questions.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Vote timing — Roll-call date and chamber are correct; times are included only when supported.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Member position — Yes, no, abstain, absent, present, excused, and source-specific positions retain their meaning.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Result and tallies — The official result and available counts are reconciled with member positions, with exceptions explained.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Source evidence — Each roll call links to its competent official publisher and retrieval evidence. A licensed intermediary can supply research leads; licensing alone does not authorize promotion as official truth.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Session coverage — Pagination, archive members, chamber partitions, and declared date scope are reconciled against the source inventory.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Durable storage — Large records are stored through supported bounded writes without dropped members, rolls, or metadata.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Reader join — Per-member votes reconnect to bill and roll metadata; successful storage alone does not pass.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Public display — A legislator’s public view displays their actual votes with bill, question, date, position, and result where available.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Missing versus no votes — No acquired record, unavailable route, and an evidenced lack of votes are distinct reader states.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Alternate route — A blocked primary route leads to documented permitted alternatives such as official bulk files, documented APIs, licensed datasets, or published journals.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Correction history — Amended official results supersede earlier versions with traceable provenance.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Sponsorship — Sponsor and cosponsor relationships retain session, bill, role, dates, and official evidence.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Bill progression — Actions, amendments, committee referrals, enactment, vetoes, and effective dates are linked without conflating a proposal with law.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Vote explanation — Published member statements are sourced and distinguished from Meanwhile summaries; no inferred political positions are manufactured.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Election identity — Date, type, jurisdiction, and stable election ID match the administering authority.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Election authority — Administering and certifying organizations are identified separately when different.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Contest inventory — Official contest list or ballot supports the included contests; pre-certification uncertainty remains explicit.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Contest and office — Each contest links to the correct office, district, term, and number of seats elected.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Lifecycle stage — Filing, certified ballot, voting, unofficial result, certified result, and term transition are distinguished.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Filing window — Published opening, closing, and candidate-certification dates are captured when available and relevant.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Candidate list — Once due, the certified candidate roster reconciles with the official ballot or certification list.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Voting deadlines — Registration, ballot request, early voting, and ballot return deadlines include jurisdiction, date, time, and authoritative source.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Voting logistics — Where offered by the product, polling locations, voting centers, mail options, and eligibility guidance match current official information.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Exact ballot scope — Address-specific ballot claims use supported precinct and ballot-style resolution; ZIP-level possibilities are not advertised as an exact ballot.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Ballot questions — Official question text, designation, applicable geography, and source are captured when questions exist.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Measure requirements — Passage threshold, official explanations, and published fiscal material retain source and applicability when shown.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Uncontested cancellation — Canceled contests and candidates declared elected without voting are not treated as missing elections.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Candidate changes — Withdrawal, substitution, disqualification, death, and write-in status update the right contest with evidence.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Results — When due and in scope, results identify unofficial or certified status, reporting time, votes, geography, and source.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Multi-winner rules — Seats elected and votes permitted are distinct; at-large contests do not invent separately numbered seats.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Ranked-choice results — Where applicable, rounds, transfers, exhausted ballots, and official outcome are preserved rather than collapsed into misleading totals.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Recounts and disputes — Published recount or certification changes are linked to the affected result and labeled by current official status.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Ballot history — Archived ballots and prior results preserve the boundaries and rules applicable at the time.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Candidate identity — Official ballot name, source identifier, and person match are verified.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Contest relationship — Office, district, election, term, and candidacy status are correct.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Incumbency — Incumbency refers to the specific office and contest; past officeholding does not automatically count.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Campaign route research — A consistent documented source protocol checks for an authentic campaign website or other public campaign channel.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Site authenticity — A found site is checked for candidate, office, election cycle, and provenance; an old campaign site is labeled historical.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Campaign contacts — Published campaign contact channels are captured separately from government office contacts.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Public statements — When found, positions are preserved as attributable, dated quotations with source links and sufficient context.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: No inferred positions — Votes, party, donors, endorsements, and third-party descriptions are not converted into unsupported candidate statements.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Equal research effort — The protocol and attempts are recorded across candidates; differences in available material do not silently reduce research effort.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: No-hit outcome — A failed search records queries, routes, dates, and limitations; it is not proof that a site or position does not exist.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Public campaign accounts — Official campaign social or video channels are authenticated and distinguished from private personal accounts.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Source corpus — Promised source material is actually readable by the relevant worker or answer system, not only listed as a filename.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Dated endorsements — If displayed, an endorsement has a named issuer, subject, date, source, and current or historical context.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Topic navigation — Readers can browse sourced statements by topic without an inferred ideology score or automated ranking of candidates.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Public event information — Published candidate forums and campaign events have correct dates, locations, sources, and cancellation status.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Filing authority — The relevant federal, state, or local campaign-finance authority and reporting regime are identified.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Committee identity — Candidate, committee, treasurer’s public official role where permitted, and filing identifiers are linked correctly.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Reporting period — Filing coverage dates, due dates, submitted dates, and report type are recorded.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Filing inventory — Required due filings are reconciled with the authority’s index; no-filing and not-yet-due are distinguished.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Receipts — Contributions and other receipts retain source categories, amounts, units, and reporting period.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Expenditures — Spending retains categories, amounts, dates, and source references where promised by the product.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Balances and debt — Cash on hand, loans, debts, and transfers are distinguished and reconciled where reported.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Amendments — Replacement filings supersede totals correctly; original and amended reports are not added together.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Donor privacy — Public filing data is handled under the project’s privacy rules; personal addresses or prohibited fields are not exposed merely because a filing contains them.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Public presentation — Displayed totals say which committee, period, filing version, and source they represent; missing data is not zero.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Independent spending — Outside spending is distinguished from candidate-controlled spending with correct beneficiary/opponent context and sourcing.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Cross-period comparison — Comparisons account for amendments, reporting windows, and committee changes rather than presenting incomparable totals as trends.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Fiscal identity — Fiscal year dates and the responsible government are recorded from an authoritative source.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Adopted budget route — The current adopted budget or official publication route is identified; proposed budgets are not labeled adopted.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Budget document — A published current budget is acquired and linked with fiscal year, version, and readable source evidence.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Responsibility — Budget proposal, adoption, administration, and oversight roles are supported by jurisdiction-specific authority rather than generic assumptions.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Amendments — Published budget amendments are linked to the adopted budget when presenting current budget figures.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Operating and capital totals — Operating and capital budgets are distinguished, with units and fund scope stated.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Appropriations — Legal spending authorizations are distinguished from actual payments and commitments.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Revenue — Revenue categories, periods, and governmental funds reconcile with published totals.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Taxes and levies — Rate, base, adopting authority, effective date, and geography are identified without giving personalized tax advice.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Expenditures — Actual spending links to fiscal period, payee where permitted, fund, category, and source.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Procurement notices — Solicitations have identifiers, scope, authority, deadlines, and status.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Contract awards — Awardee, amount, award date, term, amendments, and approving authority are sourced; a solicitation is not an award.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Debt and bonds — Authorization, issuance, outstanding principal, repayment period, and related ballot measures are distinguished.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Audits — Audit period, issuing body, report, findings, and responses retain original context and status.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Grants — Grant awards and expenditures identify funding source, recipient, period, purpose, and reported amounts.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Financial comparison — Budgets, actual spending, debt, and campaign money remain separate categories; charts do not combine them without a justified common measure.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Attendance instructions — Published public attendance, access, and registration instructions accompany relevant meetings.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Comment procedure — Where published, how and when to comment, required registration, and submission channels are recorded accurately.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Participation limits — Residency, topic, speaking-time, and deadline rules are stated only with current authoritative support.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Accessibility — Published accommodation and language-assistance contacts and lead times are retained.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Records request route — Official records custodian and request procedure are available; any real request needs its own authorization and dated tracking.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Next meeting — If Ask promises this answer, it gives the correct body, next confirmed date/time/location, and supporting source.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Representation — If promised, “who represents me” respects geographic uncertainty and links to verified offices and holders.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Last meeting — If promised, answers distinguish published outcomes from unavailable minutes and unsupported summaries.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Votes — If promised, answers identify the person, bill or motion, date, position, and source without inferring motive.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Contact — If promised, answers distinguish official office, campaign, and public participation channels.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Evidence consistency — Generated answers use the accepted current records and expose conflicts or missing information instead of filling gaps.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Citation fidelity — The cited passage or record actually supports the answer; a working link alone does not pass.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Finance answers — Answers distinguish budget authority, adopted amounts, and actual expenditures, with dates and source context.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Source identity — Publisher, host, route, record family, jurisdiction, and authority or licensing basis are identified.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Access conditions — Permission checks and relevant provider terms are followed; a permitted API is not confused with its separate website interface.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Known routes first — Relevant field-manual entries are considered before rediscovery; their applicability and age are checked.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Attempt evidence — Request target, parameters without secrets, time, outcome, and stored artifact reference are recorded.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Pagination — All required pages or cursors are traversed and reconciled; repeated or missing pages are detected.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Archive integrity — Supported archive checks detect truncated downloads and corrupt members before promotion.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Extraction accountability — Fetched documents, extracted records, dropped records, and drop reasons reconcile where the adapter supports counts; unexplained zero extraction fails.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Record validation — Identity, dates, required fields, scope, duplicates, and contradictory facts pass the active family validator.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Thin-result protection — Unexpected loss relative to source inventory or previous accepted data is explained before replacement.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Source change — Layout, schema, endpoint, or identifier changes create a diagnosed repair task rather than silent empty data.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Candidate separation — Unverified discoveries remain candidates until validated; a search snippet is not authoritative record evidence.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Idempotency — Repeating the same accepted input does not duplicate records or inflate coverage.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Last known good — Failed updates preserve prior accepted data where available and expose its age and failed-refresh status.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Licensed fallback — A paid or licensed route is used only within held rights and approved spending; its costs and provenance are recorded.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Adapter reuse — A verified vendor route is reused across compatible tenants without assuming tenant-specific fields or permissions are identical.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Durable reason — Every failed obligation has a saved, specific reason and relevant attempt evidence.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Failure classification — Temporary connectivity, permission block, extraction defect, missing mapping, missing publication, budget pause, and unknown cause are distinguished.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Next action — Each open obligation has a responsible worker or owner, a concrete next action, and a scheduled retry or review date.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Temporary failure — Connection and timeout retries are bounded, delayed appropriately, and do not create a fast loop or duplicate writes.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Persistent route failure — Repeated identical failures trigger diagnosis or another permitted route instead of being relabeled as successful effort.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Missing mappings — Venue, tenant, identity, and geography mapping errors route to the work needed to resolve the mapping.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Alternate search — Search is offered when appropriate and follows failed or insufficient known routes; useful accepted evidence is not redundantly rediscovered without a reason.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Inherited input proof — Recorded entry IDs and supplied knowledge reflect what the worker actually received, not a later reconstruction.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Knowledge use — Actions show whether the worker used, rejected with reason, or could not use supplied routes.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Learning writeback — Roles with implemented learning outputs save verified reusable findings to the shared manual with evidence and scope.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Role limitations — Roles lacking a projection or learning output are named as such; a populated manual does not prove all roles read it.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Stale learning — Changed or disproven routes can be superseded with provenance; old advice cannot silently override newer evidence.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Absence review — Negative outcomes preserve attempted routes, scope, date, and expiration; new evidence or new search capability can reopen them through an authorized process.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: No policy invention — Use active retry and absence rules; unresolved policy conflicts are reported rather than silently choosing 12 hours or 30 days.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Run traceability — Attempts and unresolved outcomes link to the run so affected work can be reviewed or requeued without deleting valid history.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Admin visibility — The operator can see the blocker, age, next action, owner, and actual retry outcome; “will retry” alone is insufficient.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Promotion receipt — Accepted records have a durable promotion/version record and correct production scope.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Reader lookup — The production reader requests the promoted record class and correct identity, jurisdiction, and period.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Joined context — Related names, titles, bill metadata, locations, and sources survive the reader join.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Visible result — The relevant map, ballot, profile, meeting card, or other existing view shows the accepted information.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Geographic labeling — Exact and possible applicability are presented consistently with the method used.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Absence wording — Missing, blocked, unpublished, verified absent, and empty results are not collapsed into “no information exists.”

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Freshness display — Relevant check times and stale-source status match the underlying evidence where the product promises them.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Cache consistency — Served data versions update through the intended publication path; a stale cache cannot hide a successful promotion indefinitely.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Failure isolation — One unavailable source does not erase unrelated accepted data or make the whole page claim everything is missing.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Working controls — Visible enabled actions have functioning handlers; unsupported actions are clearly disabled under existing product rules.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Public source access — Displayed source links open the intended supporting record where accessible; broken links are tracked.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Routine data path — Normal civic-data updates reach readers without requiring a per-state software PR; code repairs still use the normal PR process.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Accessible presentation — Changed reader views retain keyboard access, understandable labels, and usable mobile presentation; verify the actual changed surface.

definitions.label: E
definitions.requirement: Export provenance — Downloaded or shared data includes scope, version, source, and dates without secrets or prohibited personal fields.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Contact separation — Only permitted official or campaign contact information is exposed; private personal phone numbers, emails, and home addresses are excluded.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Sensitive data exclusion — No full birth dates, family details, health, religion, sexual orientation, immigration status, or private account material is collected for enrichment or exposed by this run.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Prohibited background profiling — No personal criminal, driving, divorce, bankruptcy, property, individual voter-registration, or participation-history profiles are created by this checklist.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Employer distinction — Private employment information is not added as candidate enrichment; official governmental role information remains distinct.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Equal treatment — Source standards and research protocols are consistent across political parties, candidates, and jurisdictions; sparse evidence is not a negative judgment.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Attribution — Facts, quotations, source claims, and automated summaries are distinguishable; the product does not infer motives or endorse candidates.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Secret handling — Keys, connection strings, cookies, and private environment files never enter reports, public artifacts, prompts, or Git commits.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Retention and corrections — Withdrawn or disqualified candidacies, corrected identities, and removed public material follow the active retention and correction rules with an audit trail.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Population reference — Where population is shown or used, record the Census product, vintage, geographic key, estimate, and available uncertainty; do not substitute a ZIP postal point for a Census area.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Population delivery — The public or Admin number matches its accepted reference version; unavailable population remains unknown rather than zero.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Area facts — Each About this area fact identifies its geography, date, cited source, and actual supporting record.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Body definitions — A description of a council, commission, court, or district distinguishes a general definition from that particular body's legal powers.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Government form — Charter, municipal form, and source-backed authority explain who holds the relevant power without assigning powers from a generic title.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Legal composition — Statutory seats, appointed seats, ex-officio members, voting rights, and current membership are separate facts.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Government domains — A .gov domain or vendor tenant is a discovery lead until linked to a verified government and competent record publisher.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Operational reference — Jurisdiction lists and routing references are available to the actual production workers; a missing read is distinguishable from an empty universe.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Source inventory completeness — All registered data families have a disposition: live reader, supporting input, historical/test-only, missing implementation, or not applicable with reason.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Sovereign jurisdiction — Tribal identity inventory remains distinct from reader representation; territorial overlap alone does not establish who governs the reader.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Candidate biography — Published bio text has candidate, source, collection date, and current election context; no invented biography fills a blank.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Candidate portrait — Image identifies the correct person, retains source and permitted-use evidence, passes the existing review process, and renders from its intended asset path.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Candidate link types — Government, campaign, personal-public, and social links keep their distinct labels and current/historical status.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Filed contact restrictions — Official filing addresses are not automatically safe public display fields; apply current privacy rules before storing or exposing them.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Questionnaire states — Invitation, delivery, response, verification, and public display are distinct. An invitation is neither a response nor evidence of a position. Sending requires its own authorization.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Candidate publication revisions — The statement's document version, extraction version, page or passage, date, and supersession are preserved.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Official portrait — Image bindings use the exact official identity and term; candidate and government cards do not accidentally show different people.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Committee hierarchy — Parent committee, subcommittee, chair, member roles, and service dates are supported rather than inferred from a person's general office.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Public official statements — Speech, press release, interview, or authored publication carries exact speaker, context, date, source, and quotation evidence.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Candidate-to-official bridge — Funding, votes, statements, and portraits cross between candidacy and officeholding only through a verified identity bridge, with cycle and term intact.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Action identity — Executive orders, proclamations, veto actions, and other supported official acts have a stable publisher identifier and named executive.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Action type and authority — The actual kind of act and issuing authority are preserved; a press statement is not relabeled a binding order.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Dates and changes — Signature, publication, effective date, amendment, revocation, and expiration are distinguished where published.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Action document — Signed or official source text is acquired with its attachments, readable extraction, provenance, and version.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Action scope — Jurisdiction, affected subject, and referenced law or bill remain linked to the action without invented legal effects.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Action delivery — Official cards and Ask retrieve the same supported action; undated records and held date limits are explicit.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Profile identity — The profile joins to the correct federal member using its supported identifier, such as Bioguide, not a name guess.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Dataset attribution — Dataset edition, source, required attribution, permitted use, and observation time are retained.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Categories — Category labels and definitions preserve the publisher's meaning; they are not converted into inferred policy positions.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Denominator — Statement count, included dates, exclusions, and the basis of displayed shares accompany the profile.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Record separation — What a person said, how they voted, and who funded a campaign remain separate kinds of evidence.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Profile delivery — The profile endpoint and applicable card show the accepted data and an honest missing/stale state, without rankings invented by Meanwhile.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Venue resolution — Published venue/address, reviewed corrections, geocoding result, and map point retain provenance; one venue serving many meetings is not many venues.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Recurring calendar exceptions — A recurring schedule is reconciled with actual notices, cancellations, special meetings, and changed locations.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Notice summaries — Summary links to the exact meeting and source-document version; a changed source invalidates a stale summary.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Minutes summaries — A summary is distinguishable from the minutes and from a recorded roll call; its cited source supports every material claim.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Agenda attachments — Linked staff reports, exhibits, presentations, amendments, and supporting documents receive their own acquisition and readability states.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Outcome linkage — Motions, amendments, actions, and member votes join to the correct meeting and agenda item, with outcome and unresolved joins reported.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Event overrides — Meeting-specific public-comment or attendance rules override standing instructions only with supporting notice evidence.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Service routing — A civic issue routes to the responsible office and public contact, with geographic applicability, source, and an explicit unresolved-owner state.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Records-request state — Human/offline access requirements identify the record still owed, custodian, next authorized action, owner, and follow-up date; the record does not become complete.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Official navigation — Registration, registration-status lookup, ballot lookup, and polling-place lookup point to the competent state or local election authority.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Voting model — Assigned precinct, vote center, early voting, mail return, and drop box are distinguished; a nearby location is not automatically one the reader may use.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Voting-site schedule — Each site's dates, hours, election, address, and site-specific instructions match the official source.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Address narrowing — Where an address is required, ZIP-only uncertainty is explicit; the actual route neither stores nor logs the submitted address contrary to its privacy contract.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Lookup fallback — If direct assignment cannot be established, a working official lookup and reason are shown; a website link is not a verified assigned polling place.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Measure evidence — Official measure text, plain-language summary, contested provisions, and attributed analyses remain separate, source-linked records.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Canvass and lineup — Certified or official results, primary nominees, general-election lineup, withdrawals, replacements, and uncontested races keep their lifecycle and dates.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Measure information page — The official information page for the measure is captured with its source where one exists; its absence never holds the measure back.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Measure committee sites — The committee sites for and against the measure are captured where they exist, each labeled by side and filed committee name.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Federal finance scope — Federal candidate, authorized committees, election cycle, reporting period, receipts, spending, cash, debts, and supported breakdowns preserve FEC identities and filing provenance.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: State finance scope — State-specific filing regimes, committees, reporting periods, categories, and amendments map without silently adopting federal terminology.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Local finance scope — Filing officer, committee, office/body designation, and supported transactions have exact links. Unlinked committees remain unresolved rather than assigned by name similarity.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Donor detail boundary — Any displayed donor information follows the existing donor-privacy and source rules; acquisition does not authorize a personal profile.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Money reader agreement — Ballot, official card, funding route, and Ask agree on the same target, cycle, totals, and source; failure in one authority does not erase an independent valid holding.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Breakdown reconciliation — Committee types, contribution categories, concentration displays, and nested totals state their units and denominators and reconcile without double counting transfers.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Federal key-vote selection — Curated key-vote lists state their selection scope and do not imply the member's entire voting history.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Federal recent votes — House/Senate, Congress/session, bill or question, roll ID, member ID, and date remain linked through the promoted reader.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: State publisher authority — Each supported state's official roster and roll-call source contract is identified; retired intermediary fixtures never silently fill a failed production read.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Evidence path inventory — Every supported question family names its source store, production reader, selector, identity join, evidence shape, and public response route.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Named subject — Exact person/body questions resolve correctly even outside the selected ZIP; asking about someone does not make them the reader's representative.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Ambiguity — Same-name people, similarly named bodies, split districts, and unclear dates cause appropriate narrowing rather than a guessed answer.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Agenda lookup — A specific meeting returns the clerk's actual held items and document counts; extraction failure is not an empty agenda.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Topic search — A topic question searches the applicable readable corpus and states its scope and missing documents; a no-match is not a claim that the government never discussed it.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Time and intent — Next, last, upcoming, and historical questions apply the correct event/status window; a planned vote is not a concluded outcome.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Ballot and candidates — Answers retrieve applicable contests, candidates, sourced publications, and measure evidence from the shared readers.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Campaign money — Answers distinguish federal, state, and local campaign records, preserve period and target, and never substitute public budgets.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Actions and statements — The answer uses actual held executive actions or attributed quotations; no match produces a named gap, not an inferred opinion.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Partial failure — One unavailable reader is identified without turning all otherwise valid evidence into missing data.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Actual delivery proof — Capture a representative real request and returned evidence for each supported family. A reconstructed selector result proves less than the request actually received by the answer engine.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Holding versus answer — Track separately acquired documents, successfully extracted documents, query-retrievable records, and publicly verified answers. The Ask score cannot rise merely because database rows increased.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Reactions — Reactions attach to the sourced position or contested measure provision intended by the product; incumbent and challenger buckets remain distinct.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Collection disclosure — Required acknowledgment precedes recording; collection and possible aggregate use are explained at the point required by current policy.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Store separation — Reader identity, reactions, and other collection stores have no forbidden join path; field names alone do not prove separation.

definitions.label: G
definitions.requirement: Reaction display boundary — User-facing reaction totals are not shown contrary to the current collection policy. Internal aggregate availability does not imply a public feature.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Speak Your Mind — Supported subject, district stamp, disclosure, moderation boundary, and separation from identity follow the dedicated policy; it is not evidence of an official's position.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Feedback and question demand — Intake success, review routing, and unresolved reports remain distinct from acquired civic records and accepted corrections.

definitions.label: C
definitions.requirement: Meeting alerts — If promised, verify subscription, triggering, delivery, cancellation, and privacy end to end. This audit did not establish an implemented alert-delivery pipeline; do not show a working control on that assumption.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Authority-wide acquisition — A statewide source's full applicable universe is acquired or remains explicitly owed even when the reader starts in one pilot ZIP.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Material representations — API, PDF, HTML, attachments, and published archives are reconciled when they carry distinct facts; one successful route does not retire the others.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Scheduling mode — Every source declares standing, owner-started, event-triggered, or not wired, with last success and next action. A manual promotion contract is not an automatic job.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Promotion chain — Discovery, acquired bytes, extraction, normalized record, canonical identity, validation receipt, promoted version, query retrieval, and reader verification remain separately observable.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Promotion refusal — Source, schema, identity/jurisdiction, time, meaning, horizon, absence, and dependent-reader checks preserve their actual failure or uncertainty reason and next action.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Inheritance at dispatch — A normal worker attempt records the relevant field-manual entries actually supplied, not merely what a helper could have supplied later.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Learned route use — The attempt shows whether the worker used the supplied route, what it returned, and why any additional research was needed. Necessary distinct representations are not mislabeled wasted rediscovery.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Durable learned knowledge — New scout, detective, and engineer findings reach the shared manual through the supported write path and are retrievable by the next applicable worker.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Absence expiry — Retry timing follows the current applicable policy and source contract. A generic 30-day no-progress hold cannot silently replace shorter governed rechecks; conflicts are reported and resolved, not invented away.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Deployment assets — Required geometry, portraits, reference assets, and reader inputs are present in the actual deployment; local file existence does not prove deployed availability.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Readiness denominator — Admin names the bodies, requirements, scope, and observation time behind its percentage. A state percentage must not masquerade as a ZIP percentage.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Missing read distinction — A failed store read, unsupported family, not-yet-acquired record, and supported empty result have different visible states.

definitions.label: R
definitions.requirement: Family-to-surface proof — For every claimed public family, record accepted count, eligible count, query-retrievable count, and checked public count with their respective denominators.
